alt: Q-SPARK workshop group standing together in front of a whiteboard in a Fort Lewis College computer lab
title: High school quantum workshop
caption: Students from across the Four Corners spend a day building intuition for qubits, superposition, and quantum algorithms in an FLC Engineering computer lab.

alt: Workshop group in white cleanroom coats, hairnets, and gloves posing in front of a slide about superconductivity
title: Cleanroom crew
caption: Participants gear up in cleanroom garb before touring the fabrication lab and seeing how silicon devices are actually made.

alt: Matt Welz presenting quantum concepts to students seated at computer workstations
title: Matt Welz explains quantum
caption: Sessions pair short lectures with hands-on time at the keyboard, so ideas land while students are still working through them.

alt: Dr. Jessing holding up a sample while presenting a slide on manufacturing silicon wafers to a seated class
title: Dr. Jessing talks superconductors
caption: From superconductors to wafer manufacturing, faculty connect quantum theory to the hardware students can hold in their hands.

alt: Instructor holding up a small wafer container in front of a whiteboard covered in dimension notes
title: Wafer thin
caption: A silicon wafer makes the scale real: microns on the whiteboard, and a device you can pass around the room.

alt: Students pulling on cleanroom coats, hairnets, and shoe covers in a hallway outside the lab
title: Suiting up for lab
caption: Gowning up outside the cleanroom — the first step of a lab tour most students have never had access to before.

alt: Group of students and instructors in cleanroom coats and hairnets, holding gloves, ready to enter the lab
title: Ready for the tour
caption: Gloves on, hairnets up, and a full group ready to walk the fabrication lab at Fort Lewis College.

alt: Students in cleanroom coats gathered around lab equipment under amber cleanroom lighting
title: Inside the cleanroom
caption: Under the amber lights of the photolithography bay, students watch device fabrication step by step.

alt: Instructor at a whiteboard leading a session in a bright computer lab full of students at workstations
title: Working the problem
caption: Quantum concepts get worked out on the board and then tried immediately on the machines in the room.

alt: Matt Welz walking the aisle of the Andrew J. Senti Laboratory while students work at computers
title: Summer workshop
caption: One-on-one help as students work through quantum programming exercises in the Andrew J. Senti Laboratory.

alt: Two students at a computer workstation looking toward the front of the classroom during a session
title: Learning quantum
caption: Workshops stay small enough that every participant gets time at a machine and time with an instructor.

alt: Two students working together at a computer beneath the Andrew J. Senti Laboratory sign
title: Side by side
caption: Paired work is the default: students debug circuits together and talk through what the results mean.

alt: Boden Nachtrieb and Soren Welz working at computer workstations in an FLC Engineering lab
title: Boden Nachtrieb & Soren Welz
caption: Student participants working through a quantum computing exercise during a Q-SPARK session.

alt: Dr. Jessing presenting to students seated at lab benches with a projected slide behind him
title: Classroom session
caption: Faculty-developed curriculum walks students from the basics of quantum mechanics to real applications.

alt: Dr. Jessing standing at the whiteboard asking questions of students seated around a lab table
title: Asking the questions
caption: Discussion-driven sessions: students are asked to reason out loud before the answer goes on the board.
